summary: Extend the locked Clinical Glass case journey with one staged synthetic current-ride recovery in the Care Navigator Actions panel, one visibly separate and isolated previous-trip replay, append-only assignment/history evidence, current-plan patient and caregiver version states, and role-minimized patient/caregiver/staff projections. Reuse the existing workflow store, cards, graph, timeline, static map family, responsive shell, motion controls, and profile-only workspace switcher; add no dispatch service, live map behavior, provider connection, page family, workspace, or visual-system change.
existing_design_system: docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md, ADR-0003/ADR-0004 constraints, current Clinical Glass runtime, and role-split UI at pre-handoff commit f657848fdd157969c9a392faecc12f9b14fddd0b

visual_direction.layout: Preserve /login as the only login entry, the profile dropdown as the only workspace switcher, the current StaffAppShell, the Care Navigator/Care Team split, and embedded Graph/Audit tabs. In the Care Navigator case Actions panel, replace the one-click transportation completion with a full-width CareLink coordination section. Its hierarchy is: (1) existing Transportation recovery identity/status/task metadata; (2) a compact Current ride card for the distinct September 25 trip, staged actions, required current logistics, and append-only assignment history; (3) a secondary Previous trip replay card for immutable trip carelink-prior-001 with local playback controls and its own event feed. On desktop, current recovery is the dominant left/two-thirds surface and replay is a narrower companion; below 1024px they stack Current ride first, Previous trip replay second. The Care Team Actions panel retains only clinical/readiness actions; its embedded graph/timeline may show the minimum transport dependency status needed for readiness but no provider/driver controls or detailed CareLink history. The patient finish extends PatientResolutionView with one current-plan logistics summary containing pickup/planned arrival, return, named logistics contact, plan version, Ana seen/pending, and Camila acknowledgment. CaregiverView shows only permitted current logistics and one bounded Mark logistics seen action. Transportation remains the existing read-only CareLink resource directory/static access map and receives no assignment, failure, backup, replay, or dispatch action. No combined Staff workspace, floating workspace dock, standalone graph/audit route, or new page family is introduced.
visual_direction.color: Make no palette or token changes. Use existing amber plus warning icon/text for request pending, incomplete logistics, primary failure, no option, invalidated acknowledgment, and replay paused; indigo plus label/icon for current, assigned, playing, or selected state; mint plus check icon/text only for saved complete recovery, caregiver seen for the current version, current patient acknowledgment, replay completion, and confirmed continuity; muted/line treatment for future, disabled, not-yet-visible, or historical metadata. Failed primary assignment remains visibly amber in history after backup recovery and is never recolored as resolved. Current and historical identity are differentiated by headings, trip IDs, source labels, and placement rather than a new palette. Every state retains icon and text so color is never the only carrier.
visual_direction.typography: Keep the current Outfit/Poppins/Plus Jakarta Sans/JetBrains Mono roles and scales. Use existing heading levels and compact label/value typography; stable trip, assignment, event, and plan IDs use the current mono treatment. Required truth labels are specific at their boundary: Synthetic scenario ride, Fictional provider, Planned pickup, Planned arrival, Illustrative static route, Previous scenario replay, Original scenario time, and No live GPS or provider connection. Use Assign fictional CareLink Partner A, Record primary unavailable, Select fictional CareLink Partner B, Save recovered logistics, No option available, Mark logistics seen, and Acknowledge current plan vN. Never use booked, live ETA, tracking, provider confirmed, contracted, funding approved, Uber, treatment attendance confirmed, medically cleared, or real dispatch success.
visual_direction.spacing_and_shape: Reuse current operational p-5/p-6 card padding, 10–16px radii, one-pixel/cool borders, compact shadows, metric tiles, chips, filter pills, dividers, icon bubbles, 4/8px rhythm, and 44px patient/caregiver/mobile targets. Staged actions sit in a compact ordered step list; only the currently valid action is primary and later actions remain visibly disabled with a nearby reason. Required logistics use the existing metric-tile grid: one column on phones, two columns at small/medium widths. Assignment history and replay feed are dense vertical rows using the AuditTimeline visual family, not new tables that force horizontal scrolling. The current card is visually dominant; the historical card uses the same primitives with a clear source-boundary header and never overlaps current controls.
visual_direction.component_presentation: Care Navigator current ride starts with a stable current trip ID and synthetic-source chip. The staged sequence is request created -> fictional Partner A assigned -> Partner A failed/unavailable -> fictional Partner B assigned -> recovered logistics saved. Each successful command replaces the next-action region in place and appends, never overwrites, a compact assignment/history row with provider label, assignment ID, status, actor, and fixed CT scenario time. The failed Partner A row remains above the current Partner B row. Save recovered logistics exposes the required outbound pickup window, planned arrival, return arrangement, logistics contact, and backup owner; missing any field keeps the button disabled or the result incomplete with a visible field-level reason. No option available adds an amber at-risk result and never supplies fallback values. A later failure/material change opens current plan vN+1, clears plan-dependent seen/acknowledgment presentation, and retains all earlier rows as historical evidence. The previous-trip card is headed Previous CareLink trip replay, displays carelink-prior-001 and Sep 11, 2026, then provides Play/Resume, Pause, Restart, Exit controls and a five/six-row requested -> accepted -> driver assigned -> arriving -> pickup confirmed -> completed feed. Only events up to visible progress render as active; original timestamps remain fixed. The replay card never writes into the shared current AuditTimeline. RideMap is reused only in an explicit static/offline RIDE mode: local SVG route, fixed endpoints, no tile loading, no moving GPS marker, and a visible Illustrative static route label. Patient finish reads only the current plan projection and shows Ana seen/pending and Camila acknowledged/pending as two separate labeled rows. CaregiverView removes treatment/regimen/clinical copy, shows permitted appointment logistics plus pickup/arrival/return/contact/backup and plan version, and enables Mark logistics seen only for a complete unseen current version. The Transportation workspace continues to reuse StaffResources in read-only form and visibly says that no dispatch actions are enabled. Graph and audit remain embedded: Care Navigator sees transport actions/history appropriate to coordination; Care Team sees clinical actions plus minimum readiness dependency status; neither gains a standalone graph/audit workspace.

motion.strategy: Use existing restrained workspace motion only to explain ordered local state. A newly appended current assignment/history row or replay event may use the existing short opacity/slight-rise transition once; status chips and graph edges update in place. The static route never animates a vehicle or implies GPS. Failure/recovery, version invalidation, seen, acknowledgment, exit, reset, and persistence rejection replace content in place without celebration or scroll choreography.
motion.transitions: Keep current 140–240ms control/status transitions and the existing cubic-bezier family. Replay timing is a deterministic local timer sequence with short intervals while retaining original Sep 11 timestamps. Pause cancels the pending advance and preserves the visible index; Resume continues that index; Restart cancels the current run, begins a new replay session at the first event, and keeps focus on Restart; Exit cancels the timer and collapses/returns replay to idle; workflow Reset cancels replay and restores the canonical fixture. Stale timer callbacks produce no visible transition. Current ride commands update card, permitted timeline, graph, patient/caregiver projections, and version status together from shared state rather than staggered component-local animation.
motion.microinteractions: Reuse existing hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled, and selected behavior. The active next-step button is the only primary action; completed steps become read-only evidence and future steps state their prerequisite. Command success exposes one concise polite status such as Fictional Partner A assigned or Current plan v2 saved. Primary failure and malformed persistence recovery use bounded alerts. Replay Play/Resume, Pause, and Restart leave focus on the initiating control; Exit restores focus to the opener that exposed the replay when available, otherwise the Previous trip replay heading. Completion announces Previous trip replay complete once. Ana's Mark logistics seen action leaves focus on the resulting Seen by Ana for plan vN status. Camila's acknowledgment retains the existing disabled checkbox/button treatment with an adjacent prerequisite explanation and no duplicate success on repeated commands.
motion.reduced_motion: Effective reduced motion remains the union of prefers-reduced-motion and the product motion-off control. Under either source, current history rows and replay events appear immediately at final position with no rise, graph dash/pulse, map movement, smooth scroll, confetti, or decorative hover movement. Replay still preserves ordered, keyboard-controlled readable states; its local sequence may use minimal/near-immediate intervals without skipping event order, original timestamps, pause/resume/restart/exit semantics, focus behavior, or isolation assertions.

responsive.strategy: Preserve the existing page shell from 320px and current staff sidebar-to-mobile-rail behavior. At 1024px and above, place the dominant Current ride card beside the narrower Previous trip replay card; below 1024px stack them in DOM order. Current ride metadata, required logistics, patient finish, and caregiver logistics use one column at 320–639px and two columns where space allows. Stage controls and replay controls wrap into full-width or two-per-row 44px targets on phones. Assignment/replay rows wrap IDs and timestamps inside their card; no page-level horizontal scroll, nested vertical feed, or fixed-height clipping is introduced. The embedded graph retains its existing desktop geometry and stacked mobile order; the current/replay cards do not change global shell widths or navigation.
responsive.notes: Verify 320x568, 390x844, 768x1024, and 1440x900 with default and long failure/status copy. At every width, current versus historical trip identity, plan version, failed and current assignments, original timestamps, replay controls, static/offline labels, field errors, seen/acknowledgment distinction, and focus rings remain visible. Mobile staff navigation/footer must not cover the final recovery or replay control. Patient and caregiver targets remain at least 44px; long contact/backup values wrap without obscuring their labels.

application_states: Current ride empty/open: transportation recovery exists but no synthetic request has been created; Request synthetic ride is enabled and all later controls visibly explain their prerequisites.

Request success -> primary assignment available -> fictional Partner A assigned; the current card, permitted Care Navigator timeline, and transport graph dependency read from the same state, while patient/caregiver remain pending.

Primary failure: Partner A is append-only FAILED evidence, the blocker is reopened, current logistics are incomplete, plan-dependent patient acknowledgment and caregiver-seen state are invalid, and graph/readiness remain at risk.
Backup selection: fictional Partner B is appended as the current assignment without erasing Partner A; required logistics are still incomplete until explicitly saved.

Recovered logistics editing/disabled/error/success: each missing outbound, planned-arrival, return, contact, or backup-owner field has a visible error/reason; Save remains disabled or produces no success until all required current fields exist; success shows current plan vN and all planned logistics.
No option available: an explicit amber at-risk state with next action retained; no provider, driver, pickup, map, acknowledgment, seen state, or success is manufactured.

Material change/later failure: increment to plan vN+1, preserve earlier assignment/acknowledgment/seen events as history, return current patient acknowledgment and caregiver seen to pending, and require a newly complete current plan.

Caregiver current plan unavailable/incomplete: show a quiet pending logistics card and disabled Mark logistics seen with Complete the current logistics plan first; render no clinical, regimen, labs, Epic, provider-history, or replay content.

Caregiver complete unseen -> marking seen -> seen success for exact plan vN; duplicate seen is a no-op. Seen alone changes no assignment, patient acknowledgment, clinical disposition, graph confirmation, or continuity rule.

Patient finish unavailable/incomplete: show current plan vN with explicit missing prerequisites and disabled acknowledgment. Complete current plan shows pickup/arrival, return, contact, backup, Ana pending/seen, and Camila pending; acknowledged success records only exact current version and attendance remains unknown.

Historical replay idle/empty feed -> playing requested/accepted/driver-assigned/arriving/pickup-confirmed/completed -> paused -> resumed -> complete -> repeat playback; every visible row keeps its original Sep 11 scenario timestamp.

Replay restart starts deterministically at the first event with a new local session; Exit, workflow Reset, component unmount, and persona switch cancel the active timer and return replay to idle without modifying current trip, current audit, graph, acknowledgments, or communications evidence.

Replay static/offline success: local event fixture and local SVG route render with networking disabled. If the fixture is absent/malformed, show Previous trip replay unavailable with role=alert, keep current recovery usable, and make no network fallback.

Persistence valid: hydrate and recompute derived readiness. Stale schema, malformed IDs/unions, mismatched versions/acknowledgments, impossible assignment order, replay bounds, or cross-trip references are rejected wholesale and deterministically reset to canonical start with one quiet Recovered saved scenario notice; no partially shaped success renders.

Static map default/success/offline: reserve stable dimensions, show local route/endpoints and Illustrative static route / No live GPS text; map failure falls back to a text stop list and never attempts provider, geolocation, WebSocket, XHR, fetch, SDK, or live tile recovery.

Transportation workspace: read-only CareLink directory/access map with no dispatch action. Care Team: clinical/readiness controls only. Care Navigator: transportation controls only. Profile dropdown remains the only workspace switcher.

Synchronous local commands require no network loading spinner. Button pressed/disabled feedback prevents duplicate commands; replay playing is the only ongoing progress state and is exposed as readable status rather than indeterminate loading.
Reduced-motion mode preserves all current-ride, replay, failure, reset, privacy, seen, acknowledgment, and offline states with movement removed.
accessibility: Use native buttons and form controls for every staged command, replay control, caregiver seen action, and patient acknowledgment. Keep the existing global 2px accent focus-visible outline and logical DOM/tab order: Current ride heading/status -> current next action/form -> append-only history -> Previous trip replay heading/status -> controls -> feed.

Implement the staged current ride as an ordered list with an accessible current-step label. Completed and failed steps remain readable history, while disabled future actions have visible aria-describedby prerequisite text; opacity alone never explains availability.

Group required logistics in a semantic fieldset/legend. Associate field errors through aria-describedby and aria-invalid; focus the first invalid field only after an explicit Save attempt, not during typing. A complete local save announces once through the shared polite status region.

Represent assignment history and replay events as semantic lists with provider/actor, status text, stable ID, and explicit CT scenario time. Historical replay status uses a single bounded aria-live=polite region that announces only the newly visible event or mode change, never rereads the full feed at each timer tick.

Replay controls have accurate changing names and states: Play previous trip replay or Resume previous trip replay, Pause previous trip replay, Restart previous trip replay, and Exit previous trip replay. Pause/Resume/Restart never move focus; Exit restores the opener when possible; completion is announced once and repeat playback remains keyboard reachable.

Current and historical maps have an accessible text equivalent naming pickup and destination plus the exact statement Illustrative static route; decorative SVG paths/markers are aria-hidden. No moving marker, unlabeled animation, or live-location announcement is present.

Every requested, assigned, failed, recovered, pending, seen, acknowledged, playing, paused, complete, invalidated, and unavailable state combines icon, label, and structural treatment with color. Failure/recovery meaning remains understandable in forced colors and at 200% zoom.

Ana's seen state and Camila's acknowledgment are separate labeled rows with actor, exact plan version, and fixed scenario time where applicable. Copy explicitly says Caregiver visibility does not replace patient acknowledgment and Seen does not indicate clinical clearance.

Role minimization applies to rendered and accessible output: Care Navigator and Transportation omit the exact clinical concern, nurse notes/disposition, regimen, labs, and Epic context; caregiver also omits treatment name and provider assignment history. Care Team receives only the transport dependency summary required for readiness, not transport mutation controls.

The patient acknowledgment control has a visible disabled reason for each prerequisite family: clinical disposition, complete current logistics, and current version. Repeated acknowledgment or seen commands produce no duplicate live announcement or event.

Persistence rejection and replay fixture failure use concise role=alert once; deterministic reset success uses polite status. Do not use alerts for each timed replay event or ordinary disabled prerequisites.

At 320px and 200% zoom, controls wrap without overlap, card content follows reading order, replay feed and assignment history require no horizontal scrolling, and the sticky/mobile navigation does not cover focused controls.
Reduced-motion behavior removes animation without removing ordered replay status, announcements, focus restoration, semantic progress, or any available control.
assets_or_dependencies: Reuse React 18, strict TypeScript, the existing WorkflowState/workflowReducer persistence boundary, current task/graph/timeline/patient/caregiver components, RideMap fallback SVG family, Lucide icons, Tailwind utilities, and current CSS tokens/components.

Add one small typed local synthetic CareLink fixture/module for distinct current-trip and immutable carelink-prior-001 replay facts only if needed; all names, IDs, timestamps, route points, providers, driver, and logistics remain reviewed synthetic repository data.

Add no image, font, runtime package, state store, animation library, map/provider SDK, API route, database table, backend contract, service worker, WebSocket, geolocation, live tile dependency, vendor integration, or network fallback. EPIC-001 capture files and behavior remain untouched.

Do not change the existing ACCESS/ML evidence.

Matched current capture plan after implementation: Care Navigator 1440x900 at request, primary assigned, primary failed, backup selected/incomplete, recovered plan, and no-option states; assignment history must retain the failed primary. Capture 390x844 staged controls, validation/disabled reasons, keyboard focus, and no horizontal overflow.

Replay capture plan: desktop and mobile idle, playing midway, paused, complete, restarted-first-event, exited, offline, and reduced-motion frames. Show carelink-prior-001, Previous scenario replay, original Sep 11 timestamps, illustrative static route, and no live GPS/provider language in-frame.

Cross-role capture plan after recovered plan: Care Navigator current trip/history; Care Team Actions plus embedded readiness graph/timeline; patient finish with current pickup/arrival/return/contact plus Ana seen/pending and Camila acknowledgment; caregiver permitted logistics/seen action; Transportation read-only resources. Compare accessible text as well as screenshots for forbidden clinical/Epic content.

No-drift constraints: do not change global CSS/tokens, fonts, header/footer, login routes, profile dropdown switcher, staff shell/nav, landing loop, existing motion preference semantics, Epic capture/assets, ML surfaces, graph/audit page ownership, or Transportation read-only behavior. Do not add a floating dock, combined Staff workspace, or standalone graph/audit workspace.

Implementation should extend the existing types/state reducer/selectors and pass explicit minimized projections into presentation components. Do not pass full WorkflowState into caregiver or transport-specific child surfaces once projections are available, and do not let components manufacture fallback provider, driver, date, pickup, return, contact, backup, seen, or acknowledgment values.

Use separate stable identities for the current September 25 synthetic recovery and historical carelink-prior-001. Current commands and selected finish must never read a historical replay field; replay progression must never append to current audit/timeline or communications evidence.

Implement append-only assignment/history and material-plan-change semantics in the single reducer: current failure/additional plan change increments planVersion, invalidates both exact-version patient acknowledgment and caregiver seen, preserves historical events, and recomputes readiness. Caregiver seen is not part of isContinuityPlanConfirmed.

Historical playback uses one cleanup-safe component timer driver plus persisted replay status/index/session token only. Reject stale callbacks by trip/session; cancel on Pause, Restart, Exit, Reset, unmount, and persona switch. Timer handles never enter persisted state.

Selected RIDE paths must force RideMap's local static/offline rendering even near the viewport. Zero ride action may perform fetch, XHR, WebSocket, provider SDK, geolocation, live tile, callback, or other dispatch/provider request. Existing non-RIDE resource-map behavior is not evidence of dispatch and must not be described as such.

Persistence validation must bump the scenario schema and reject stale, malformed, cross-version, duplicate-ID, impossible-order, mismatched-acknowledgment, invalid-replay, and cross-trip payloads wholesale. Reset only the named synthetic scenario/replay and leave Epic capture, ML evidence, OUTREACH attempt limits/results, and provider evidence untouched.

Focused implementation/tests should cover every acceptance path plus exact rendered privacy boundaries, field-by-field incomplete logistics, no-option at risk, duplicate/out-of-order no-ops, acknowledgment/seen invalidation, offline static rendering, zero provider-network calls, replay fake timers/control sequences/stale callbacks, deterministic persistence reset, and byte-for-byte current-state isolation during replay.
